ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a plank $B$ with mass $m_{B}=14\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on a horizontal ground, and a crate $A$ with mass $m_{A}=10\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on plank $B$. A light rope is tied to the crate at one end and to the ground at the other end. When the rope is taut, it makes an angle of $\theta=37^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between crate $A$ and plank $B$ is $\mu_{1}=0.5$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between plank $B$ and the ground is $\mu_{2}=0.4$. The gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. A horizontal force $F$ is applied to pull plank $B$ out from under crate $A$ at a constant speed. Find the required force $F$. (Given: $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$)

1. The magnitude of the tension $T$ in the rope.
2. The magnitude of the tension force $F$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows plank B resting on a rough horizontal ground. Crate A sits on top of plank B. A rope is attached to crate A and runs down toward a ground anchor on the left, making an angle θ = 37° with the horizontal. A horizontal external force F pulls plank B to the right. Reasoning following separate free-body diagrams: For crate A: plank B is being pulled right underneath A, so the kinetic friction exerted by B on A is to the right. The rope tension T acts along the rope toward the left and downward, so its components on A are T cos37° leftward and T sin37° downward. Vertically, A has no acceleration, so the normal force from B on A is N1 = mA g + T sin37°. Horizontally, A is in balance, so μ1 N1 = T cos37°. Substitute mA = 10 kg, g = 10 m/s², μ1 = 0.5, sin37° = 0.6, cos37° = 0.8: 0.5(100 + 0.6T) = 0.8T. Thus 50 + 0.3T = 0.8T, so 0.5T = 50 and T = 100 N. Then N1 = 100 + 0.6(100) = 160 N, and the friction between A and B is μ1N1 = 0.5(160) = 80 N. For plank B: crate A exerts a leftward friction force of 80 N on B. The ground normal on B supports both B's weight and the downward normal from A, so N2 = mB g + N1 = 14(10) + 160 = 300 N. The kinetic friction from the ground on B is leftward with magnitude μ2N2 = 0.4(300) = 120 N. Since plank B is pulled at constant speed, horizontal forces on B balance: F = 80 + 120 = 200 N.
